summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to let taxpayers deduct interest paid on loans for certain new U.S.-assembled recreational motorboats by adding them to the definition of applicable passenger vehicles eligible for the personal loan interest deduction.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates a new tax deduction but does not authorize or alter any direct government outlays or programs. It therefore has no bearing on government spending levels.

The core purpose of the bill is to expand the deductibility of personal loan interest to include qualifying watercraft, directly reducing taxable income for affected taxpayers and thereby lowering their federal tax liability.
No provisions relate to health insurance, medical care, or healthcare financing.
No provisions address firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.
No provisions address visas, border security, or immigration pathways.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions affect military budgets, procurement, or defense policy.
The bill references the Clean Air Act definition for motor vehicles but makes no changes to environmental standards or regulations for boats or any other vehicles.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net benefits.
No provisions address schools, student aid, or education policy.
No provisions address controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill explicitly excludes watercraft and motor vehicles whose final assembly did not occur in the United States, creating a domestic-content preference that favors protectionist trade policy.
By expanding a tax deduction, the bill reduces federal revenue and thereby increases the deficit relative to current law, moving away from debt-reduction priorities.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions address voting access, election administration, or voter ID.
No provisions address data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance.
No provisions address collective bargaining, worker protections, or union rights.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
